Reforms in Orissa jails
*21. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
cash-starved state of Orissa has not been
able to carry out the desired reforms in
their jails; and
(b) whether the Central Government
propose to render financial or other help
to overcome this handicap; if so, the
details thereof, if not the reasons therefor?
Dialogue with elected representatives
to resolve Kashmir issue
*22. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Union Government is of
the view that there is need for a dialogue
with the elected representatives and the
separatist groups to resolve the Kashmir
issue
(b) if so, whether any steps have been
taken or being taken in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Special drive to detect and deport
foreigners
*23. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government
have asked the State Governments to
launch a special drive to detect and deport
11,500 Pakistanis overstaying in India
after the expiry of their travel documents;
(b) whether similarly the silent and
continuous intrusion into India by 20
million illegal Bangladeshis is a matter
of concern;
(c) what concrete steps are proposed
to be taken to deport these illegal
intruders;
(d) the number of persons from
Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and other
countries’ citizens who are overstaying in
India as on 1.1.2003;
(e) whether anyone of them is
suspected to be involved in terrorist
activity; and
(f) if so, details thereof and steps taken
to nab them?

Withdrawal of subsidy on power
consumption by farmers
*24. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Central
Electricity Authority has proposed
withdrawal of subsidy on power
consumption by farmers;
(b) whether it is a fact that the State
Governments are unable to implement the
CEA's proposal as they are facing a lot of
resistance from the farmers who are
already reeling under drought and other
natural calamities and non-remunerative
prices for their agricultural produce; and
(c) if so, the reaction of the Central
Government thereto?
Communal clashes in the country
*25. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of communal clashes
that took place during the last one year;
(b) the number of persons killed and
injured in these clashes; and
(c) the details of steps taken by
Government to enhance communal
harmony?
Controversy over application of
POTA in U.P.
*26. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH
LIBRA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
note of the controversy arising out of the
recent application of POTA in Uttar
Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details of the case and
views of the State Government thereon;
(c) whether Centre propose to forward
some advice to the State Government on
this development; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Schemes for supply of drinking water
to Himachal Pradesh
*27. SHRI ANIL SHARMA: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the schemes sanctioned for
providing pure drinking water in rural,
backward and snow-bound areas of
Himachal Pradesh during the last five
years;
(b) the year-wise amount released in
this regard to Himachal Pradesh by the
Central Government during the last five
years; and
(c) the amount spent by Himachal
Pradesh on their own during the said
period?
Over crowding in jails
*28. SHRI B. J. PANDA:
SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the reports captioned, "Indian jails
overcrowded with 67,000 prisoners—UP
jails worse with over 29,000 inmates,
Jammu and Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Manipur
prisons have space" as reported in the Asian
Age, dated the 18th December, 2002;
(b) if so, the factual position about
over-crowding in different jails and
whether National Human Rights
Commission has expressed concern over
this; and

9
WIN2\SESSION\7295RS.pm5 9
(c) the position with regard to over-
crowding in jails in Orissa with steps to
reduce this?
Funding for rural development
programmes
*29. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the States
have not only diverted but also reneged
on their share of funding key rural
development programmes to the tune of
a colossal Rs. 150 crore in 2001-2002 as
against total dues of Rs. 2020.48 crore;
(b) if so, who were the biggest
offenders in this regard;
(c) the action proposed to be taken
against these States;
(d) whether as on November 12, 2002
another 2,17,211 habitations are being
supplied with unsafe drinking water; and
(e) what are the efforts being made to
provide safe drinking water and ensure
utilisation of the funds fully provided by
the Centre?
National Electric Power Survey
*30. SHRI LALITBHAI MEHTA:
Will the Minister of POWER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 15th
National Electric Power Survey carried
out by Central Electricity Authority
projected the need for capacity
augmentation by 55000 MW for the Tenth
Plan;
(b) if so, the reasons for targetting the
augmentation of 41100 MW during
Tenth Plan; and
(c) what steps are being taken to bridge
the energy deficit during Tenth Plan period
in the country?
Breach in PM's security
*31. SHRIMATI N. P . DURGA:
PROF. SAIFUDDIN SOZ:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there have been some
incidents where security lapses have
occurred in Prime Minister's security;
(b) if so, the number of such cases
during the last one year; and
(c) what foolproof steps have been
taken to ensure perfect security?
Jawans of Delhi Police at the disposal
of retired police officers
†*32. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as on
September last year, 1200 jawans of Delhi
Police were at the disposal of serving and
retired police officers of Delhi Police for
private work;
(b) if not, the number of such jawans
who were at the disposal of such serving
and retired police officers of Delhi Police;
and
(c) the total annual amount spent on the
salaries and allowances of such jawans?
Fixing the number of BPL families
for States
*33. SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH
LIBRA:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

10
WIN2\SESSION\7295RS.pm5 10
(a) whether Centre has fixed the number
of Below Poverty Line (BPL)  households
for States and told them not to exceed this
limit while conducting the census to
identify such families;
(b) if so, whether  Government are
aware that with several States reeling under
severe drought, the BPL  figures have
soared and the Centre's move is bound to
keep several families out of the list of
beneficiaries;
(c) whether some Chief  Ministers
have  written  to  Centre  in  this  regard;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Dual citizenship to NRIs residing in
Gulf countries
*34. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to offer dual citizenship to
the People of Indian Origin who have
settled abroad;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Government are thinking not to offer dual
citizenship to some of the NRIs residing
in some of the Gulf countries;
(c) if so, the details of the countries
which have been barred from this offer;
and
(d) the reasons for denying dual
citizenship to Indians who are residing in
those countries?
Peace talks with Naga leaders
*35. SHRI V. V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI MANOJ BHATTA -
CHARYA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether NSCN (I-M) leaders came
to India and met the Prime Minister and a
few other Ministers of the Government in
January this year;
(b) if so, the details of the talks and
the purpose of the visit;
(c) whether the secessionist leaders
pressed  for  the  grant  of  greater
Nagaland  as  a  pre-condition  for  peace
in the N.E. Region and if so, the details
thereof and Government's reaction
thereto; and
(d) what was the final outcome
thereof?
Wind and bio-gas energy
†*36. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
for giving boost to wind energy/bio-gas
energy;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Mukherjee Commission on
disappearance of Netaji
Subhas Chandra Bose
*37. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Mukherjee
Commission set up to inquire into the
disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra
Bose has sought for an extension of time
to  complete  its  work  and  submit  its
report;
(b) if so, the details thereof and reasons
therefor; and
(c) Government's reaction thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

WIN2\SESSION\7295RS.pm5 11
MIG-21 crash in Srinagar
*38. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a MIG-
21fighter aircraft of the IAF crashed in
the outskirts of Srinagar on 26th
December, 2002;
(b) if so, the number of casualties
thereon;
(c) whether any terrorist organisation
claimed their hand in the incident;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether any inquiry was
conducted; and
(f) if so, details of the inquiry report?
Financial assistance to private power
distribution companies
*39. SHRIMATI SHABANA AZMI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of POWER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether private power distribution
companies have got fresh financial
assistance from the Centre to implement
their upgradation plans and develop
infrastructure;
(b) if so, whether in the month of
September, 2002, companies got their first
instalment of Rs. 400 crore as aid from
the Centre;
(c) if so, what is the total aid that has
been provided to the private power
distribution companies by the Centre so
far; and
(d) to what extent these companies
have utilised these funds to improve the
power sector?
Action plan for Panchayati
Raj bodies
*40. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is
preparing a national action plan for the
elected representatives and development
functionaries of Panchayati Raj bodies;
(b) if so, the objectives
thereof;
(c) whether State Governments
have been consulted before the formation
of this action plan; and
(d) by when it is likely to be
implemented?

Disinvestment of three units
of C.I.L.
†102. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that three units
of  Coal India Ltd. i.e. ‘Eastern Coal Fields
Ltd.’, ‘Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.’ and ‘Central
Coal Fields Ltd.’ are incurring losses
continuously for the last three years;
(b) if so, the number of years for which
each unit is incurring loss;
(c) to what extent these units have
incurred losses, so far;
(d) whether Government have
considered any proposal to hand over the
management of these units to the private
sector by making disinvestment therein; and
(e) if not, the details thereof?
Cost of coal production in India
†103. SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that production
cost of Coal India Limited, a monopoly
Public Sector Undertaking, is more than
the cost of production at international level;
(b) if so, the average cost of production
of coal at international level;
(c) the average cost of production of Coal
India Ltd. in India;
(d) whether efforts have been made
during previous years to bring coal
production industry at par with international
level; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Strike by Singareni Coal Mine
workers
104. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Singareni Coal Mine
workers are on warpath and have served
strike notice against privatisation; and
(b) if so, the action taken to apprise
workers about their future and job
protection besides cre ating confidence
amongst Trade Unions?

25
WIN2\SESSION\7297RS.pm5 25
Closure of ECL Mines
105. SHRI RUMANDLA RAAMA-
CHANDRAYYA: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Union
Government has not yet taken any specific
decision on the closure of 22 mines of the
Eastern Coalfields Limited;
(b) if so, whether the Union Government
is making efforts to review seriously and
find scope to make these viable;
(c) whether the reports published
recently about the closure of these mines
have been contradicted by the Ministry; and
(d) if so, by what time final decision in
this regard is likely to be taken?
Mine blast casualties
106. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA:
SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMED
KHAN (DURRU):
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Indian troops posted
along the 1800 mile border between India
and Pakistan, while withdrawing from their
positions, left behind the mines laid by them
along the border;
(b) if so, whether any more casualties
due to mine blasts have since taken place
along the border;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken to remove the mines
and to prevent any casualties therefrom?
Steps to boost the morale of Army
Troops
107. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is  a fact that the Indian
Army is suffering from acute fatigue on
account of counter-insurgency operations
in Jammu  and Kashmir and Operation
Parakram; and
(b) the action proposed to ensure health
maintenance of Army Troops and boost their
morale?
Non-utilisation of defence funds
108. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it has been reported in the
Economic Times dated the 23rd December,
2002 that Rs. 3,000 crore kept for weapons
is lying unutilised, so far;
(b) if so, what were the main reasons
for not utilising the fund for purchase of
weapons;
(c) whether any inquiry has been
conducted in this regard;
(d)  if so, who are responsible for this
and action taken against them;
(e) whether the Centre has now taken a
final decision to utilise this amount for
purchase of weapons during 2003; and
(f) if so, to what extent weapon deals
have been finalised by now?

26
WIN2\SESSION\7297RS.pm5 26
Transparency in defence deals
†109. SHRI P. K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the steps taken to bring transparency
in defence deals after the revelation of facts
in the film made by the tehelka.com on
alleged kickoff in the defence deals;
(b) the details of the new policy made to
check the kickoffs in defence deals;
(c) to what extent the said new policy
has been successful; and
(d) the number of defence deals in which
this new policy has been implemented?
Aircraft carrier deal with Russia
110. SHRI RUMANDLA RAAMA-
CHANDRAYYA: Will the Minister of
DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Russia have
finalised the deal of aircraft carrier for the
Indian Navy;
(b) if so, whether any agreement in this
regard has been signed;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) by what time the agreement is likely
to be implemented?
CVC report on defence deals
111. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether CVC has submitted its final
report to Government on defence deals; and
(b) if so, what action Government have
taken on the findings of CVC?
Modernisation of Indian Army, Navy
and Air Force
112. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a large amount totalling to
Rs. 3,000 crores for purchase of weapons
is lying unutilised;
(b) if so, reasons for not utilising the
amount; and
(c) details of the measures taken by
Government to modernise Indian Army,
Navy and Air Force?
Indo-French Strategic Dialogue
113. SHRI C. O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the ninth round of Indo-
French Strategic Dialogue was held in
New Delhi; and
(b) if so, the details of the agreements
reached?
Punching of driving licences of traffic
violators
114. SHRI BHAGATRAM
MANHAR: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
“Licences of traffic violators to be punched
from January 30,” appearing in the
Hindustan Times, New Delhi dated the
9th January, 2003;
(b) if so, what are the complete details
of the scheme to be implemented from
30th January, 2003;
(c) whether Government are aware that
Delhi Police is challaning citizens arbitrarily
on petty offe nces like jumping of roads,
etc.; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

WIN2\SESSION\7297RS.pm5 27
(d) if so, whether Government would
punch the licences without giving ample
opportunity to the drivers and if not, the
reasons therefor?
Deterioration of Law and Order
situation in NCT of Delhi
115. SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
SHRI BHAGATRAM
 MANHAR:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that law and order
situation in the National Capital Territory of
Delhi has deteriorated during the last one
year;
(b) if so, the details of cases of rape,
murder, extortion, dacoity etc. reported in
various police stations during the above
period;
(c) whether it is also a fact that cases of
extortion and murder have increased in
Malviya Nagar area of South Delhi during
the last one year; and
(d) if so, the details of cases reported
and what steps Government have taken or
propose to take for the safety of residents in
and around Malviya Nagar area?
Assault on an American missionary
116. SHRI V. V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
SHRI C.O. POULOSE:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the physical assault on an
American missionary, Mr. Joseph Cooper
in Trivandrum;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken to book the culprits and punish them;
(c) whether it is a fact that Mr. Cooper
has been ordered to leave the country for
allegedly violating the visa rules;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the action taken to ensure that foreign
citizens abide by the restrictions and do
not violate the laws of the country?
Rules for Pakistani Nationals visiting
India
117. SHRI ABANI ROY:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Union Government have
recently announced stricter rules for
Pakistanis visiting India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether a large number of Pakistani
visitors have not gone back to their country
even on the expiry of visa period in the
past few months;
(d) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(e) the number of such Pakistani visitors
missing in the country and also the number
of such persons who came on fake visas;
and
(f) the concrete steps taken to search
such persons and to deport them to Pakistan?
Restriction on movement of Pakistani
Nationals
118. SHRI MANOJ BHATTA-
CHARYA: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently
decided to restrict the movement of Pakistani
Nationals to three Indian cities only;
(b) if so, the details thereof and reasons
therefor; and

28
WIN2\SESSION\7297RS.pm5 28
(c) whether Pakistan has taken any
reciprocal step in this direction and if so,
the details thereof?
Crimes against women in Delhi
119. SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMED
KHAN (DURRU):
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the capital, Delhi continues
to hold the position of the capital of crimes
against women particularly rapes and
murders combined with rapes; and
(b) if so, the number of rapes and rapes
with murders in Delhi, as compared to
the Capitals of different States, till
November, 2002 and the corresponding
figures for 2001 and 2000?
Security arrangements in the country
120. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY:
SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
 Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country
is facing grave internal security threats;
(b) whether Government have taken a
final stock of its efforts to restructure the
security arrangements in the country in the
wake of attack on Indian Parliament on
December 13, 2001;
(c) if so, the results thereof;
(d) whether in Government's perception,
there is a definite improvement in the security
environment in the country and if so, the
details thereof; and
(e) what steps are being taken in this
regard?
Economic package to the people of
Kashmir
121. SHRI AIMADUDDIN
AHMED KHAN (DURRU):
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of India have
taken any decision to grant an economic
package to the people of Kashmir by way
of generating employment opportunity for
the growth, including jobs for the over-aged
youths and other means for bringing the
misguided youth, who have taken to guns
and militancy, into the national mainstream;
and
(b) if so, the details of the package and
the cost thereof indicating the Central aid
to be extended therefor?
Dual citizenship to PIOs
122. SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU:
SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY:
SHRI MANOJ BHATTA-
CHARYA:
SHRI R.P. GOENKA
SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
SHRI BHAGATRAM
MANHAR:
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision to confer dual citizenship on the
People of Indian Origins currently settled
in other countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) the specific rights, privileges as
benefits which are proposed to be made
available to PIOs as a result of grant of dual
citizenship;

29
WIN2\SESSION\7297RS.pm5 29
(d) the benefits likely to accrue to India
as a result thereof; and
(e) by when the legislative and
administrative framework are likely to be
put in place?
Committee set up for solving problems
of PIOs
123. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have appointed
a Committee for solving the problems of
NRIs and People of Indian Origins;
(b) if so, whether the committee has
submitted its report to the Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the basic
recommendations made by Government
including the dual citizenship for NRIs; and
(d) the steps being taken by Government
for providing the dual citizenship to NRIs
who are working for strengthening India's
economy?
Over-crowding in Tihar Jail
124. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Tihar Jail
which has a total capacity of 3637 inmates,
was having 12,041 prisoners as on
31st December, 2002 and that nearly similar
conditions prevail in all the jails in the
country;
(b) if so, whether any study has been
made in the recent past as to how this over-
crowding could be eliminated, either by way
of adding more jails or by resorting to
speedy trials; and
(c) if so, what effective steps are being
taken in this regard?
Request for UAVs by Andhra Pradesh
125. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Andhra Pradesh had
requested for assistance for equipping its
police force with Unmanned Air Vehicles
(UAVs) to check extremist activity; and
(b) if so, the reaction of the Union
Government thereto?
Foreign aids to terrorist activities
†126. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the fund for carrying out
terrorist activities in the country and
